title: The Fridge Map Nobody Reads
sendTrigger: Save this for your next fridge clean-out.
editorialNotes: Slide 2 repeats slide 1 layout (hero-statement): both are two-sentence hooks; same constraint as post 41.
The 7-10°F door-temperature gap is stated without a source in the brief; kept as a list item, never hero type.
Brief colors the door zone Signal Red as "wrong"; thread palette here is Steel Blue and Ink Gray because no slide declares a loss figure.

thread.element: line-art fridge cutaway filling in one zone per slide
thread.endState: fully labeled five-zone map compressed to a corner badge

copy.headline: Your fridge came with a place to put everything. Most of those places are wrong.
The egg holder is built into your door. That's the worst spot in the whole fridge for eggs.
The door opens dozens of times a day.
items: Every open lets warm kitchen air in.
The door runs 7-10°F warmer than the back of the fridge - closer to room temperature than to "cold storage."

copy.headline: Bottom shelf, back: the coldest zone in the fridge - this is where raw meat and fish belong.
copy.body: It also keeps any drips contained below everything else, instead of dripping onto food you won't cook first.

copy.headline: Middle shelf: dairy, eggs, leftovers.
items: Consistent mid-range cold, easy to see, easy to rotate.
Top shelf: the least perishable stuff - drinks, ready-to-eat items, leftovers you'll finish today.

copy.headline: Crisper drawers aren't interchangeable.
items: High-humidity setting = leafy greens and herbs (they wilt when they lose moisture).
Low-humidity setting = fruit (it rots faster in trapped moisture).

copy.headline: The fridge isn't one temperature. It's five zones.
fond tracks shelf life by what's actually in each zone of your fridge - not a generic countdown.
